newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on selective buying.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse ended higher on Friday as both domestic and foreign investors bought selective stocks on hopes that a hike in petroleum prices would be delayed, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive index closed 9.41 points higher at 779.87.
"The market showed some firmness but hence the fate of the market will depend on the hike in petroleum product prices," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
Prime Minister Inder Gujral met Finance Minister P. Chidambaram and Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu on Thursday to discuss measures needed to plug a mounting oil subsidy bill.
The 15-member United Front coalition, which Gujral heads, is in a dilemma over raising state-controlled prices. The Front's steering committee is meeting on May 25 to discuss oil prices.
Reliance Industries closed 2.45 rupees higher at 294.95.
State Bank of India rose 1.75 rupees to 305.
Larsen and Toubro gained 1.40 rupees at 213.55.
